spans.s: Mṛga, pl. (ºāḥ), the brahmans in Śākadvīpa. § 575b (Śākadvīpa): VI, 11, 436, 437 (brāhmaṇabhūyishṭhāḥ; only C., B. has Maṅgāḥ).
mṛga, pl. (ºāḥ) (“deer”). § 127 (Aṃśāvat.): I, 66, 2626 (the offspring of Mṛgī). Do.^2 = Śiva (1000 names^1) (ºpakshiṇaḥ).
Mṛgaśiras, name of a nakshatra, v. Su. Si. § 759 (Ānuśāsanik.): XIII, 110, 5394 (description of the cāndravrata). Cf. Mṛgottama.
Mṛgamandā, daughter of Krodhavaśā. § 127 (Aṃśāvat.): I, 64, 2624, 2626 (mother of the bears and the sṛmaras).
Mṛgasvapnanidarśana (“the dream of the deer”). § 11 (Parvasaṅgr.): I, 2, 471 (Dharmarājasya cātraiva mºṃ, i.e. Mṛgasvapnodbhavaparvan).
Mṛgasvapnodbhava (“the dream of the deer”). § 10 (Parvasaṅgr.): I, 2, 324 (i.e. Mṛgasvapnodbhavaparvan).

Mṛgasvapnodbhavaparvan (“the dream of the deer,” the 44th of the minor parvans of Mhbhr.). (Cf. Mṛgasvapnanidarśana, Mṛgasvapnodbhava.) § 518: In consequence of a dream of Yudhishṭhira, in which the still remnant deer of Dvaitavana entreated him to spare them by changing his residence, the Pāṇḍavas with Indrasena, etc., and the brahmans removed to the Kāmyaka forest, situated at the head of the desert, near lake Tṛṇabindu. They had then dwelt in Dvaitavana during a year and eight months (III, 258).
Mṛgavyādha^1, a Rudra. § 108 (Aṃśāvat.): I, 66, 2566 (son of Sthāṇu).--§ 191 (Arjuna): I, 123, 4825 (among the Rudras present at the birth of Arjuna).
Mṛgī (“hind”). § 127 (Aṃśāvat.): I, 66, 2624 (daughter of Krodhavaśā), 2626 (mother of the deer (mṛgāḥ)).
Mṛgottama, a nakshatra (= Mṛgaśiras, PCR.). § 749 (Ānuśāsanik.): XIII, 89, 4257.
